rulings.docket_item: P18-006 (Jer.49.19-Jer.49.22): rule the Jer.49.19|Jer.49.20 cut, and arbitrate the recorded cross-lens factual tension over what pmarks carries at MT 49:19.
rulings.grounds: ARBITRATION OF THE PMARKS TENSION (inventory bytes, controlling): pmarks_Jer.json records ONE entry at that key, marks[Jer.49.19] = SAMEKH - a setumah, single-witness (WLC/OSHB), tier-3 WEAK in the Prophets. Chapter 49 carries seven entries and every one is SAMEKH (MT 49:6, 49:11, 49:19, 49:22, 49:27, 49:33, 49:39); no PE stands anywhere in the chapter, so PE is never in play here and is not conflated. The inventory's own key convention is fixed by those bytes: five of the seven key to the verse immediately BEFORE a nation header (MT 49:6 before the Edom header at 49:7, MT 49:22 before Damascus at 49:23, MT 49:27 before Kedar at 49:28, MT 49:33 before Elam at 49:34, MT 49:39 before the Babylon header at 50:1), so an entry keyed to MT V stands at the V|V+1 edge. The MT 49:19 setumah therefore stands at the Jer.49.19|Jer.49.20 edge - inside the span as drawn - and NOT at the Jer.49.18|Jer.49.19 edge; nothing is keyed to MT 49:18, and that absence is never counterevidence. Both lenses' facts are inventory-true; the lens reading the entry as interior to the drawn span is the correct one, and the row's front seam carries no mark of any type. Tier-3 corroborates; it decides nothing. TIER-1 GROUND (which alone decides): oshb:Jer.49.20 opens verse-initially לָכֵ֞ן שִׁמְע֣וּ (byte tier) - a consequential particle plus a second-person-plural discourse-frame imperative, the enumerated tier-1 internal-seam class - and the frame owner turns with it: oshb:Jer.49.19 closes וּמִי זֶ֣ה רֹעֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲמֹ֖ד לְפָנָֽי (byte tier), first-person divine speech, while 49:20 speaks of Yahweh in the third person. The second witness agrees, closing its quotation at the end of 49:19 and carrying “Therefore hear the counsel of Yahweh, that he has taken against Edom” (web:Jer.49.20) outside it. The drawn front edge carries nothing of the kind: oshb:Jer.49.19 opens הִ֠נֵּה כְּאַרְיֵ֞ה (byte tier), a presentative plus simile - no word-event shape, no lamed-initial or non-lamed OAN header, no koh-amar, no vocative, no imperative, and not among the classified date-candidate sites. The row's stated ground for declining the seam is byte-false: the question series terminates at 49:19's verse-final accent, so nothing runs past the verse boundary. Tier-1 evidence therefore stands at the declined edge and is wholly absent at the drawn one, and the seam belongs at Jer.49.19|Jer.49.20. FORM OF THE ADOPTION: installed as a seam MOVE, not a split. A split (Jer.49.19-Jer.49.19 plus Jer.49.20-Jer.49.22) would leave the device-less Jer.49.18|Jer.49.19 edge standing as a row seam, which is the very defect being cured, and would add a row and cascade the chunk index. The move warrants both resulting seams and costs the tiling nothing. COUNT OBJECT NAMED (the reviewers used different objects): the controlling object is leading identical whitespace tokens on the maqaf-free staged extract; the digits are 9 for oshb:Jer.49.19 against oshb:Jer.50.44 (diverging at the tenth token, plene אַרְגִּ֤יעָה against defective אַרְגִּ֤עָה) and 7 for oshb:Jer.49.20 against oshb:Jer.50.45 (diverging at the eighth, אֱד֔וֹם against בָּבֶ֔ל), both byte tier. The challenge's 7 and 6 name a maqaf-joined token object and understate the run under the staged extract, which is maqaf-free at every tier.

consequence.spec: ADOPTED SPAN SET (two rows, no row added, no row retired, no chunk_index change): P18-005 respans Jer.49.14-Jer.49.18 -> Jer.49.14-Jer.49.19 (unit_type nations_oracle, parent_collection M10 Jer.46.1-Jer.51.64, chunk_index_in_book 233 unchanged); P18-006 respans Jer.49.19-Jer.49.22 -> Jer.49.20-Jer.49.22 (unit_type nations_oracle, parent_collection M10 Jer.46.1-Jer.51.64, chunk_index_in_book 234 unchanged). TILING: neighbors are unchanged (P18-004 Jer.49.12-Jer.49.13 before, P18-007 Jer.49.23-Jer.49.27 after), the pair remains contiguous, no frame seam is straddled (both rows stay wholly inside M10), and 1364/1364 survives; re-confirm with check_tiling.py --range Jer.49.1-Jer.50.46. P18-006 EDITS: boundary_rationale rewritten to open on לָכֵ֞ן שִׁמְע֣וּ (oshb:Jer.49.20, byte tier) as the row's own onset, naming the class (verse-initial second-person-plural discourse-frame imperative) and the frame-owner turn from first-person divine speech to third-person speech about Yahweh, with “Therefore hear the counsel of Yahweh, that he has taken against Edom” (web:Jer.49.20); the setumah keyed to MT 49:19 is cited as front-edge corroboration and the setumah keyed to MT 49:22 as the row's own close, each labelled single-witness and tier-3 weak in the Prophets. DELETE the sentence-continuation clause from boundary_rationale AND the matching clause from strongest_rejected_alternative - both are byte-false and neither may reappear in any form. strongest_rejected_alternative is rewritten to engage the rival of holding Jer.49.19 with the counsel material as one unit, answered on 49:19's verse-final close. observed_substrate_signals becomes [speech_formula.discourse_imperative, narrative_frame.addressee_shift] - the refrain key is dropped as texture, not an onset class. confidence re-rated with a bespoke rationale (the two tier-1 signals at the onset support medium). literature_type_guess re-cut to the counsel-and-eagle material actually spanned. P18-005 EDITS: boundary_rationale extended to carry the lion-simile close, הִ֠נֵּה כְּאַרְיֵ֞ה (oshb:Jer.49.19, byte tier), disclosing that no tier-1 device stands at that verse's onset - which is why it is held inside this unit rather than opening one - and citing the setumah keyed to MT 49:19 as this row's own closing corroboration (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets). strongest_rejected_alternative, literature_type_guess and confidence re-rated to the six-verse span. SEAM-PAIR CURE - ONE EDIT INSTALLED ON BOTH ROWS: disclose the lion-from-the-Jordan template pair straddling the adopted seam, with its object, digits and tier - leading identical whitespace tokens on the maqaf-free staged extract, 9 for oshb:Jer.49.19 against oshb:Jer.50.44 and 7 for oshb:Jer.49.20 against oshb:Jer.50.45, byte tier, diverging at the tenth and eighth tokens respectively - and disclose that this tiling reads Jer.50.44-Jer.50.46 as one unit and that the seam adopted here is NOT extended there, the internal stanza seams of the Babylon material being held open at reduced confidence. The variant asymmetry is disclosed from the inventory: one ketiv/qere note stands at MT 50:44 and none at MT 49:19 (single-witness). SWEEP SCOPE (E-18): this ruling is decision-local and expressly NOT a corpus-wide order. No row in Jer.50.1-Jer.51.64 is touched, altered or re-rated by it; P18-029 (Jer.50.44-Jer.50.46) stands unchanged. DOCKET WORK ORDERS: the P18-006 remedy's two deletion clauses are ABSORBED (both fields are rewritten wholesale); its 'replace the warrant with the parallel-treatment ground' clause is SUPERSEDED - the parallel recurrence converts from a not-cutting warrant into the cross-seam disclosure specified above; its 'disclose that no tier-1 device stands at Jer.49.19 and that no parashah entry is keyed to MT 49:18' clause is SUPERSEDED as to the vacated edge and re-installed on P18-005 as the held-inside disclosure; its single-witness/tier-3 labelling clause and its confidence re-rating clause STAND and are executed on both rows. Any standing work order from another slice addressed to P18-005 or P18-006 prose is executed on the respanned row, not voided.

rulings.docket_item: P18-009 (Jer.49.32-Jer.49.33): TWO-option respan - (i) Jer.49.28-Jer.49.33 entire, or (ii) a cut at Jer.49.29|Jer.49.30. Adopt exactly one or decline both.
rulings.grounds: OPTION (ii) IS ADOPTED. The standing seam does not survive re-derivation: oshb:Jer.49.32 opens וְהָי֨וּ גְמַלֵּיהֶ֜ם (byte tier) - third-person report with no speech formula, no header of the lamed or non-lamed class, no word-event shape, no date element, no vocative and no imperative; the inventory puts no parashah entry between the setumah keyed to MT 49:27 and the setumah keyed to MT 49:33, and no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note at MT 49:31 or MT 49:32 (paseq at MT 49:12, 49:24, 49:28, 49:37, 49:39; K/Q at MT 49:25, 49:28, 49:30, 49:36, 49:39 - all single-witness). The only signal at that edge is a shift out of imperative address into report, and the row already crosses that same shift one verse-pair earlier without cutting: oshb:Jer.49.29 opens אָהֳלֵיהֶ֤ם וְצֹאנָם֙ יִקָּ֔חוּ (byte tier), third-person, immediately after the imperatives of 49:28. A class applied inconsistently inside a row's own span cannot warrant that row's seam, and the row's opening sentence denying an addressee shift is false on the bytes either way. WHERE THE TIER-1 CONFIGURATION ACTUALLY STANDS: at Jer.49.30, and two enumerated classes stand there together. oshb:Jer.49.30 opens verse-initially נֻסוּ֩ נֻּ֨דוּ מְאֹ֜ד (byte tier), second-person-plural discourse-frame imperatives, and carries the explicit vocative יֹשְׁבֵ֥י חָצ֖וֹר (oshb:Jer.49.30, byte tier) - the addressed party turning from the attackers commanded at oshb:Jer.49.28 ק֚וּמוּ עֲל֣וּ (byte tier) to the victims addressed at 49:30, with the named target turning from Kedar to Hazor and tracking the header's own dual naming, “Of Kedar, and of the kingdoms of Hazor” (web:Jer.49.28). Discourse-frame imperatives and explicit addressee shifts are both enumerated tier-1 internal-seam classes, and vocatives are named again in the OAN-block internal-cut rule. WHY OPTION (i) IS NOT TAKEN: it is lawful but it is the null option. It would erase the tier-1 configuration standing at 49:30, retire a row and cascade chunk_index_in_book across every later row in the book; and the ground that most recommends it - that the setumah pair keyed to MT 49:27 and MT 49:33 brackets 49:28-49:33 with nothing keyed between - is tier-3 weak and single-witness, which under the owner addendum cannot decide against a tier-1 seam any more than it could in a challenge or a defense. Option (ii) lands the seam on the classes owner law names, and costs the tiling nothing. K/Q CHECKED BEFORE QUOTING (inventory first): MT 49:28 carries one ketiv/qere note, on the king's own name - the ketiv writing the plene byform against the qere's dominant resh-family spelling, standing as a doubled token in the verse bytes, נבוכדראצור נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֣ר (oshb:Jer.49.28, byte tier) - and MT 49:30 carries one further note; both single-witness. Neither verse is one of the twelve doubled-note verses. The header splice is לְקֵדָ֣ר וּֽלְמַמְלְכ֣וֹת חָצ֗וֹר (oshb:Jer.49.28, byte tier).

consequence.spec: ADOPTED SPAN SET (two rows, no row added, no row retired, no chunk_index change): P18-008 respans Jer.49.28-Jer.49.31 -> Jer.49.28-Jer.49.29 (unit_type nations_oracle, parent_collection M10 Jer.46.1-Jer.51.64, chunk_index_in_book 236 unchanged); P18-009 respans Jer.49.32-Jer.49.33 -> Jer.49.30-Jer.49.33 (unit_type nations_oracle, parent_collection M10 Jer.46.1-Jer.51.64, chunk_index_in_book 237 unchanged). TILING: neighbors unchanged (P18-007 Jer.49.23-Jer.49.27 before, P18-010 Jer.49.34-Jer.49.38 after), the pair remains contiguous, no frame seam is straddled, 1364/1364 survives; re-confirm with check_tiling.py --range Jer.49.1-Jer.50.46. P18-009 EDITS: STRIKE the opening sentence asserting that the spoils continue without an addressee shift. boundary_rationale is rewritten so its warrant is located AT the adopted seam and checkable there - נֻסוּ֩ נֻּ֨דוּ מְאֹ֜ד (oshb:Jer.49.30, byte tier) opening verse-initially with the vocative יֹשְׁבֵ֥י חָצ֖וֹר (oshb:Jer.49.30, byte tier) and the target turning to Hazor - and closes on the desolation formula at 49:33 with the setumah keyed to MT 49:33 as corroboration (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets). Disclose the one ketiv/qere note at MT 49:30 (single-witness), consulted per the inventory. strongest_rejected_alternative is rewritten to engage the strongest rival - reading Jer.49.28-Jer.49.33 as one header-bounded unit, bracketed by the setumah pair keyed to MT 49:27 and MT 49:33 with nothing keyed between - and to answer it on the verse-initial imperative-plus-vocative at 49:30. observed_substrate_signals becomes [narrative_frame.addressee_shift, speech_formula.discourse_imperative, refrain.sodom_gomorrah_formula]. confidence LOWERED from high to medium; frontier_flag_considered set true. literature_type_guess re-cut to the Hazor half of the oracle. P18-008 EDITS: boundary_rationale re-cut to the two-verse span - the fourth lamed-initial header לְקֵדָ֣ר וּֽלְמַמְלְכ֣וֹת חָצ֗וֹר (oshb:Jer.49.28, byte tier), the koh-amar and the go-up command ק֚וּמוּ עֲל֣וּ (oshb:Jer.49.28, byte tier), and the spoils notice closing at 49:29 - with the front-seam setumah keyed to MT 49:27 (single-witness, tier-3 weak) and the one paseq seg at MT 49:28 (single-witness, count-only, position not recorded). The 49:28 royal-name ketiv/qere disclosure is retained. strongest_rejected_alternative, literature_type_guess and observed_substrate_signals ([oan_header.lamed_initial, speech_formula.koh_amar]) re-cut to the new span; confidence re-rated with a bespoke rationale. SEAM-PAIR CURE - ONE EDIT INSTALLED ON BOTH ROWS: disclose the byte-true devices straddling the adopted seam - (a) the go-up imperative pair, ק֚וּמוּ עֲל֣וּ (oshb:Jer.49.28) against ק֣וּמוּ עֲל֗וּ (oshb:Jer.49.31), each byte tier at its own verse but the RECURRENCE between them at accent_stripped/skeleton tier only, the two accent patterns differing; (b) the camel token, וּגְמַלֵּיהֶ֖ם (oshb:Jer.49.29) against גְמַלֵּיהֶ֜ם (oshb:Jer.49.32), byte tier at each site, accent_stripped across the pair; and (c) the king's name recurring at MT 49:28 (ketiv plene byform beside the qere) and MT 49:30 (resh-family spelling), the name form named before any digit. Each disclosure names its tier; none may be carried at byte tier as a cross-site recurrence. ALSO DISCLOSED, NOT CUT: the second verse-initial go-up imperative at oshb:Jer.49.31 stands INSIDE the respanned P18-009 and is held there rather than opening a further unit; say so in one clause. DOCKET WORK ORDERS: the P18-009 remedy's 'strike the no-addressee-shift sentence' clause is ABSORBED; its 'state what stands at Jer.49.31|Jer.49.32' clause is SUPERSEDED - that edge is now interior to P18-009 and owes no seam warrant, and its instruction to disclose that no tier-1 device falls there must NOT be executed, since a shift out of imperative address into report does stand there and the row may not assert its absence; its 'rewrite strongest_rejected_alternative to address the seam actually drawn' clause is ABSORBED by the respan and satisfied by the rival named above; its confidence/frontier clause, its accent_stripped-or-skeleton tier clause for the imperative bracket (now mandatory as part of the seam-pair cure), and its single-witness/tier-3 parashah labelling clause all STAND and are executed on both rows. SWEEP SCOPE (E-18): decision-local; no corpus-wide order issues from this ruling and no row outside P18-008/P18-009 is altered.

rulings.docket_item: P18-026 (Jer.50.35-Jer.50.38): respan Jer.50.33-Jer.50.38 as one koh-amar-headed unit, absorbing the row into its predecessor, as against keeping the cut with the ordered disclosures.
rulings.grounds: THE PROPOSAL'S PREMISE RE-DERIVES AS TRUE. oshb:Jer.50.35 opens חֶ֥רֶב עַל כַּשְׂדִּ֖ים (byte tier) with no koh-amar, no hoy, no vocative, no imperative and no date element; its only formula token is the mid-verse neum, which is closure corroboration and never an onset. oshb:Jer.50.33 does open verse-initially on כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (byte tier), a tier-1 koh-amar onset with the tsevaot title. The construct chain straddles the row's own front seam undisclosed: לְיֹשְׁבֵ֥י בָבֶֽל closes oshb:Jer.50.34 against וְאֶל יֹשְׁבֵ֣י בָבֶ֔ל at oshb:Jer.50.35, byte tier at each site. The sword digit re-derives as five tokens over three verses - one at MT 50:35, two at MT 50:36, two at MT 50:37 (skeleton tier, TOKEN counts, MT keys) - and oshb:Jer.50.38 opens חֹ֥רֶב, sharing skeleton and accent with the litany's own word and differing in the first vowel alone. Mark disclosure inside MT 50:35-50:38 is owed nothing: the inventory records no parashah entry, no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note in that range (ch 50 marks at MT 50:5, 50:7, 50:16, 50:17, 50:21, 50:27, 50:30, 50:32, 50:46; paseq at MT 50:14, 50:29, 50:34; K/Q at MT 50:6, 50:8, 50:11, 50:15, 50:29, 50:44 - all single-witness, tier-3 weak where marks are concerned). So the seam is under-warranted at tier-1 and under-disclosed, exactly as found. THE PROPOSAL IS NEVERTHELESS DECLINED, ON OWNER LAW RATHER THAN ON THE BYTES. The Jer.50.34|Jer.50.35 edge is an internal stanza seam of the 50-51 Babylon complex - the region the owner gate names as expected-low-confidence and expressly NEVER decides, to be held honestly at a reduced-confidence posture with bespoke rationale. Adopting the respan would decide that seam; so would ratifying the cut. A boss ruling applies that hold, it does not consume it, and no tier-1 signal in the span is strong enough to override an owner-ruled hold in either direction. The disposition therefore stays where the peer left it: the cut stands, un-ratified, at a reduced-confidence held-open posture, carrying the ordered disclosures. NOT AN ESCALATION: the item asks whether to adopt a boundary change in a region owner law holds open, and applying the hold answers it. No owner-law provision needed reinterpretation to reach this result.

consequence.spec: The respan is NOT adopted. No span, unit_type, parent_collection, chunk_index or row-count change follows from this ruling; P18-025 stays Jer.50.33-Jer.50.34 and P18-026 stays Jer.50.35-Jer.50.38, and 1364/1364 is undisturbed. THE DOCKET'S EXISTING WORK ORDER STANDS UNCHANGED and is stated here in full so nothing is lost with the declined proposal: (1) the seam-pair cure - ONE edit installed at both ends - disclosing the yoshvei-Bavel construct chain straddling the Jer.50.34 | Jer.50.35 seam with its swept object, unit, digit and tier, installed on P18-026's device_notes AND on P18-025 which closes at Jer.50.34; (2) strongest_rejected_alternative on P18-026 replaced so it engages the continuous reading from the Jer.50.33 koh-amar onset rather than the Jer.50.38 split, and answers it on bytes; (3) boundary_rationale's sword sentence re-cut to the bytes - one sword token at Jer.50.35 governing the Chaldeans and, through the prepositional chain, the inhabitants of Babylon, her princes and her wise men, with four further tokens heading their own clauses at Jer.50.36-Jer.50.37 (sweep: 5 tokens over 3 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys); (4) confidence lowered to medium_low with a bespoke rationale naming the undisclosed cross-seam chain and the held-open posture for the internal stanza seams of this material. ADDED BY THIS RULING: nothing. The four ordered edits are sufficient, and item (2)'s rival is precisely the reading declined here, so the author answers it on the bytes recorded above without treating this declination as ratifying the seam.

rulings.docket_item: P19-006 (Jer.51.25-Jer.51.32): rule the 51:26|51:27 seam itself - adopt an exact change, or decline.
rulings.grounds: THE CONFIGURATION IS REAL AND STRONGER THAN THE ROW ADMITS. oshb:Jer.51.26 closes verse-final on נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (byte tier), and oshb:Jer.51.27 opens verse-initially on שְׂאוּ נֵ֣ס בָּאָ֗רֶץ (byte tier), heading a series of six second-person-plural commands read from the pointed bytes and matched by six commands in the second witness (web:Jer.51.27) - against the singular addressee running through 51:25-26 (oshb:Jer.51.25 opens הִנְנִ֨י אֵלֶ֜יךָ הַ֤ר הַמַּשְׁחִית֙, byte tier, with singular address and singular suffixes continuing to 51:26). A verse-initial discourse-imperative series is itself an internal-seam class, and the same class opens a unit at oshb:Jer.51.45 צְא֤וּ מִתּוֹכָהּ֙ עַמִּ֔י (byte tier) in this very stretch; the byte-grade closure standing verse-final one verse earlier is exactly the condition under which the ruled treatment lets that formula do closure work. The tiling already treats the identical configuration as a seam one verse-pair before, where verse-final נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.51.24, byte tier) is followed by the addressee shift at 51:25. THE CITATION DEFECT IS CONFIRMED: the two-word pair the row carries under a byte-tier label at oshb:Jer.51.27 does not stand there at all - 51:27 opens with the imperative - and reaches byte tier only at oshb:Jer.51.12, where it splices the nomen rectum of the governing phrase onto the following imperative, אֶל חוֹמֹ֨ת בָּבֶ֜ל שְׂאוּ נֵ֗ס (oshb:Jer.51.12, byte tier). The form the two verses actually share is שְׂאוּ נֵ֣ס at 51:27 against שְׂאוּ נֵ֗ס at 51:12 - the same two words differing in the accent on the second, so the recurrence holds at accent_stripped tier, not byte. THE SEAM IS NEVERTHELESS NOT ADOPTED, ON OWNER LAW. Jer.51.26|Jer.51.27 is an internal stanza seam of the 50-51 Babylon complex - the region the owner gate names as expected-low-confidence and expressly NEVER decides, to be held at medium_low/low with bespoke rationale. Adopting a cut there would decide a held-open seam; the peer referred and did not decide for the same reason. Applying the hold is not reinterpreting it, so this is a declination and not an escalation. BUT THE ROW MAY NOT BE LEFT WITH A BYTE-FALSE NOT-CUTTING WARRANT. The docket orders the author to say why a verse-initial imperative series does not cut here when the same class opens a unit at 51:45, and supplies no lawful answer; the only answer available on the bytes is the held-open posture, and any formulation asserting that no device stands at 51:27, or resting the holding-together on the flanking parashah pair, is false or tier-insufficient. A cure beyond the docket's existing order is therefore installed.

consequence.spec: No span, unit_type, parent_collection, chunk_index or row-count change; P19-006 stays Jer.51.25-Jer.51.32 and 1364/1364 is undisturbed. The docket's existing four boundary_rationale orders STAND (delete the two-word catchword citation; re-cite the shared form spliced separately from each site with the cross-site tier named accent_stripped and the digit re-attached to that object - sweep 4 verses book-wide, 4:6, 50:2, 51:12, 51:27, 2 of them in this chapter; re-cut the 51:27 pairing to the splice extent or extend the splice through the trumpet clause; cite the byte-grade closure verse-final at oshb:Jer.51.24 as the onset-side warrant and disclose the second closure verse-final at oshb:Jer.51.26, with the flanking parashah marks demoted to tier-3 single-witness corroboration). ADDED CURE (this ruling, beyond that order): boundary_rationale must state the not-cutting ground AFFIRMATIVELY and in internal-seam vocabulary, in three parts. (a) NAME the tier-1 internal-seam class that DOES stand at the seam: a verse-initial second-person-plural discourse-imperative series at oshb:Jer.51.27, six commands, spliced שְׂאוּ נֵ֣ס בָּאָ֗רֶץ (byte tier), with the addressee number turning from the singular address running through 51:25-26 to plural - the form-class labels argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings, since no morphology layer is staged. (b) NAME the byte-grade closure standing verse-final immediately before it, נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.51.26, byte tier), and say that closure corroboration is available there because a fresh onset follows. (c) REST the holding-together on the reduced-confidence, deliberately undecided posture this unit already carries for the internal stanza seams of this material - not on any absence claim and not on the flanking marks. PROHIBITED FORMULATIONS (the cure fails if any survives): that no tier-1 device stands at 51:27; that neither half carries a formula 'of its own' as the reason for holding them together (a parent-header test applied to an internal seam); and any warrant that would equally deny the seam at Jer.51.24|Jer.51.25 or at Jer.51.44|Jer.51.45, both of which this tiling cuts on the same classes. confidence stays medium_low and frontier_flag_considered stays true; observed_substrate_signals is unchanged, the three declared keys all being attested in the span. CURE TEST: every Hebrew citation re-collates at the ref it is placed against at the tier claimed; every digit names the object it counts and its unit; and the not-cutting warrant, applied to this stretch, distinguishes 51:27 from the verse-initial imperative onsets the same stretch does cut by the held-open posture and by nothing else.

rulings.docket_item: P20-002 (Jer.52.4-Jer.52.11): rule the proposed cut at 52:6.
rulings.grounds: RULED FROM THE BOOK'S OWN SEAM CLASSES ONLY. The 2 Kgs 24:18-25:30 parallel to this appendix is typed-relation metadata and decides no Jeremiah seam; it is not used here, in either direction. THE BYTE FACTS CONFIRM: oshb:Jer.52.6 opens verse-initially and asyndetically on בַּחֹ֤דֶשׁ הָֽרְבִיעִי֙ בְּתִשְׁעָ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ (byte tier), a month ordinal plus day, with the famine clause following; the span quotes and dispositions nothing from that verse, and its categorical no-fresh-date wording is falsified by that notice standing inside the span. THE CUT IS DECLINED FOR WANT OF AN ESTABLISHED TIER-1 SIGNAL. The ruled date-formula-onset class is a byte-defined object of 19 classified candidate sites, and 52:6 is not among them: the notice carries no year word and is invisible to that object's sweep. The inventory's own adjacent-shape list gives per-site reads for oshb:Jer.52.1, oshb:Jer.52.5 and oshb:Jer.52.12 and is silent on 52:6, so no class membership is established for it. Nor does any second tier-1 signal stand at the edge: no participant is newly named, no addressee or scene changes, and the clause dates a CONDITION inside the siege the verse-initial year-bearing frame at oshb:Jer.52.4 וַיְהִי֩ בַשָּׁנָ֨ה הַתְּשִׁעִ֜ית לְמָלְכ֗וֹ (byte tier) opened - a siege whose terminus the preceding verse has just stated, עַ֚ד עַשְׁתֵּ֣י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.52.5, byte tier), so the chain is explicitly continuous across 52:5|52:6. Contrast the one edge in this chapter that this tiling does cut on a month-and-day shape: oshb:Jer.52.12 וּבַחֹ֤דֶשׁ הַֽחֲמִישִׁי֙ בֶּעָשׂ֣וֹר לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ (byte tier) carries the same shape but is paired with a newly named agent entering the account, a second and independent tier-1 signal that 52:6 has not got. The parashah layer is silent through the whole chapter but for a petuchah keyed to MT 52:30 (single-witness, tier-3 weak), and that silence is never counterevidence in either direction; the English paragraph break at 52:6 is tier-4 and carries no weight. Under the owner addendum an adopted boundary change needs an affirmative tier-1 warrant at the seam, and none is established. EXPRESSLY NOT SETTLED, AND NOT NEEDED TO RULE: whether a yearless verse-initial month-and-day notice belongs to the ruled date-onset class. The declination rests on the absence of any established tier-1 warrant AND on the absence of any second signal, so the definitional question is untouched and stays open. Recorded, not escalated, because ruling this item did not require reinterpreting the class.

consequence.spec: The cut is NOT adopted. No span, unit_type, parent_collection, chunk_index or row-count change; P20-002 stays Jer.52.4-Jer.52.11, its neighbors P20-001 (Jer.52.1-Jer.52.3) and P20-003 (Jer.52.12-Jer.52.16) are untouched, no frame seam is straddled (all three stay wholly inside N11), and 1364/1364 is undisturbed. THE DOCKET'S EXISTING WORK ORDER STANDS UNCHANGED, restated in full: replace the categorical no-fresh-date wording in strongest_rejected_alternative and boundary_rationale with a per-site reading that names oshb:Jer.52.6, quotes its verse-initial month-and-day run at byte tier, and states why it is read as internal to the siege the 52:4 frame opens - the same per-site treatment the row already gives the terminus at 52:5; name the shape and its year-word absence in device_notes; add oshb:Jer.52.6 to boundary_evidence_refs. Confidence and frontier flag are the author's to re-rate against that disclosure. ADDED BY THIS RULING: nothing. CURE TEST unchanged and sufficient: no categorical claim about dates survives that a dating notice standing inside Jer.52.4-Jer.52.11 falsifies, and every date-shaped verse inside the span - oshb:Jer.52.5 and oshb:Jer.52.6, the only two - is dispositioned per-site with its bytes quoted.

rulings.docket_item: CWO-5 policy ruling: may a declared closure-classed observed_substrate_signals key name a device outside the declaring unit's own span? Enumerate the declaring rows from the frozen corpus and rule ONE scope policy.
rulings.grounds: DETERMINISTIC ENUMERATION (swept from SP/Jer/draft_rows_combined.jsonl, 276 rows; the swept object is the observed_substrate_signals key speech_formula.neum_closure, named before any digit): 10 declaring rows - P05-002 Jer.13.12-Jer.13.14, P05-013 Jer.15.5-Jer.15.9, P07-007 Jer.21.11-Jer.21.14, P08-001 Jer.23.1-Jer.23.8, P08-002 Jer.23.9-Jer.23.15, P08-004 Jer.23.23-Jer.23.32, P09-002 Jer.25.8-Jer.25.14, P09-004 Jer.25.30-Jer.25.33, P18-007 Jer.49.23-Jer.49.27, P18-024 Jer.50.31-Jer.50.32. Six of the ten close on a verse carrying no neum token: P08-001 (MT 23:8), P08-002 (MT 23:15), P09-002 (MT 25:14), P09-004 (MT 25:33), P18-007 (MT 49:27), P18-024 (MT 50:32). The census matches the docket exactly. COUNT OBJECTS NAMED AND BOTH TESTED (E-05, and the test that corrected this ruling's own first pass): object A is the CONTIGUOUS two-word run neum-YHWH, skeleton tier, verse counts, MT keys - 162 verses, matching the inventory digit; object B is the bare neum TOKEN, skeleton substring, verse counts, MT keys - 169 verses, matching the inventory digit. Object B controls, because the key claims a token and the title-stack shapes are their own count objects. The two objects agree on which six rows fail at the close, so the consequence set is object-independent; they do NOT agree on where the support lies, and object A alone would have produced two false statements here. At MT 51:57 object A misses what object B finds, the melekh-signature stack standing between the two words. At MT 50:31 object A likewise misses the stack נְאֻם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָא֑וֹת (oshb:Jer.50.31, byte tier), which is one of the four adonai-stack sites - so P18-024, which object A shows as having no support anywhere in its span, in fact has support at its own opening verse. WHERE THE SUPPORT ACTUALLY LIES, per consequence row (neum-token verses inside each span under object B, MT keys): P08-001 MT 23:1, 23:2, 23:4, 23:5, 23:7; P08-002 MT 23:11, 23:12; P09-002 MT 25:9 and 25:12, both mid-verse and neither closing anything, with a further token one verse OUTSIDE and before the span at MT 25:7; P09-004 MT 25:31; P18-007 MT 49:26, the tsevaot stack נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.49.26, byte tier), standing one verse before the row's own close; P18-024 MT 50:31, its opening verse. EVERY one of the ten therefore has support somewhere in its own span, and no row's support is exclusively out-of-span. That is decisive for how the policy must be worded: a span-level test alone clears all ten and settles nothing, so the operative bar has to be the verse-level test the P09-002 cure names - present in the verse it is claimed of - which is what separates the four sound rows from the six. GROUNDS FOR THE POLICY CHOSEN. (1) The ruled treatment makes the closure formula corroboration ONLY, closing a unit where a fresh tier-1 onset follows - a mechanism that attaches to the unit's own CLOSE. A token at the opening verse, or mid-verse in the middle of a span, or before the front seam, does no closure work for the declaring unit; a token before the front seam does that work for the PREVIOUS unit. (2) observed_substrate_signals is a record of the declaring row's own observed substrate and a dependent field of its drivers; a signal that stands outside the span is not this row's substrate at all. (3) The campaign already settles the same architecture for a weaker layer: parashah keys are BARRED from the field and their corroboration is carried in prose only. Out-of-span and off-close corroboration belongs in the same place. (4) Permitting qualified out-of-span keys would leave the field un-checkable by any span-scoped validator and would multiply disclosure text without adding evidence. The out-of-span arm of the policy is stated for completeness; no consequence row in this sweep turns on it.

consequence.spec: POLICY RULED (option (i), bind-or-drop, with the P09-002 cure test as the operative bar): a closure-classed observed_substrate_signals key is valid ONLY where the device it names stands in the DECLARING UNIT'S OWN CLOSING VERSE. In-span-but-not-closing support does not license it; out-of-span support NEVER licenses it. Where the key is dropped, the device is disclosed in prose with its verse ref and tier - never re-encoded under another key. CONSEQUENCE ROWS AND THE EDIT EACH TAKES (one edit per row): P08-001 Jer.23.1-Jer.23.8, P08-002 Jer.23.9-Jer.23.15, P09-002 Jer.25.8-Jer.25.14, P09-004 Jer.25.30-Jer.25.33, P18-007 Jer.49.23-Jer.49.27, P18-024 Jer.50.31-Jer.50.32 - each DROPS speech_formula.neum_closure from observed_substrate_signals, and each adds one sentence to boundary_rationale stating that its closing verse carries no closure formula and naming what actually closes the unit; where the token stands elsewhere in the span or before the front seam, that position is named in prose with its MT ref and byte tier and is NOT re-encoded as a key. P09-002's sentence states that the close rests on the recompense clause completing the sentence begun at 25:8, וְשִׁלַּמְתִּ֥י לָהֶ֛ם כְּפָעֳלָ֖ם וּכְמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.25.14, byte tier), that its two in-span tokens at oshb:Jer.25.9 and oshb:Jer.25.12 stand mid-verse and close nothing, and that the token at oshb:Jer.25.7 stands outside the span and before its front seam. P18-024's sentence states that its only in-span token stands at its OPENING verse, oshb:Jer.50.31, in the adonai-stack shape - its own count object, four sites book-wide - and not at its close. P18-007's states that its token stands at oshb:Jer.49.26, one verse before the close, in the tsevaot stack shape. Where dropping the key leaves the row's driver set thinner, the dependent fields re-open with it: strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type and confidence are re-checked on each of the six. ROWS UNAFFECTED (key stands unchanged, device attested in the closing verse): P05-002, P05-013, P07-007, P08-004. CURE TEST each consequence row must pass: no closure-classed key survives in observed_substrate_signals whose named device is absent from the row's closing verse under the 169-verse neum-token object (skeleton tier, MT keys); and the prose sentence names the closing verse, states the absence, and names what closes the unit instead. SWEEP SCOPE (E-18): this order is carried to execution as its OWN sweep over observed_substrate_signals in draft_rows_combined.jsonl, scoped to the single key speech_formula.neum_closure (10 declarations). It is NOT folded into any row's fix and does NOT reach the sibling closure-classed keys, which are named here with their digits for a SEPARATE sweep under the same policy: speech_formula.neum_yhwh_closure, 6 declarations, 2 consequence rows (P02-004 Jer.4.14-Jer.4.18, close MT 4:18; P02-011 Jer.5.10-Jer.5.13, close MT 5:13); divine_title.neum_yhwh_closure, 6 declarations, 0 consequence rows. The three non-neum closure-classed keys (date_frame.narrative_date_closure, narrative_frame.speech_closure_transition, narrative_frame.summary_closure, 1 declaration each) name devices the neum objects cannot test and are outside both sweeps; they need their own named object before any digit.

MY OWN RULINGS THIS ROUND PRODUCED ZERO OWNER ESCALATIONS. Each of the five span items was decided by APPLYING a stated provision, not by reinterpreting one: B4-1 and B4-2 applied the enumerated tier-1 internal-seam classes (discourse-frame imperatives, explicit addressee shifts, and the OAN-block vocative rule) together with the tier-3 weight rule for the parashah layer; B4-3 and B4-4 applied the owner-ruled hold on the internal stanza seams of the 50-51 Babylon complex, which answers an adopt-or-decline question without consuming the hold; B4-5 applied the byte-defined date-onset object and the requirement that an adopted change carry an affirmative tier-1 warrant. B4-6 was a scope question the docket expressly delegated as boss-decidable and was settled inside the existing field contract and the ruled closure mechanism, not against them. It did not have to be settled to decline the 52:6 cut, and legislating it would have exceeded the item; it is recorded here so that it is visible if the shape recurs, not raised as a question requiring an answer this round.
